_meta.description: Security architecture for the commercial bank platform following a zero-trust model. Covers the six observable security posture controls surfaced in the Observability Aggregator dashboard, the mTLS service-to-service authentication model using SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity, a six-level data classification scheme with per-service assignments, five-zone network segmentation, and three architectural design decisions. All policy is version-controlled in service.yaml manifests and enforced at runtime by Istio and the Zero-Trust Policy Engine (SVC-113).

security_posture_controls.name: Zero-Trust Policy Map
security_posture_controls.description: Overlay on the container diagram showing for each service: what it is allowed to call (from service.yaml), what it actually calls (from Istio/Envoy telemetry), and the diff. Any observed call not in policy = security finding. Any allowed call never made = dead policy to remove (least privilege). Data source: service mesh access logs via OTel Collector → Zero-Trust Policy Engine.

security_posture_controls.name: mTLS Edge Status
security_posture_controls.description: Every connection between services carries encryption status from service mesh telemetry. Green = mTLS (mutual TLS, both sides authenticated). Amber = TLS only (encrypted but no mutual auth). Red = plaintext — immediately actionable. Derived from Istio access log fields.
security_posture_controls.data_source: Istio access logs via OTel Collector

security_posture_controls.name: Secret Rotation Age
security_posture_controls.description: secret_expiry_seconds Prometheus gauge per secret. Green = rotated within window. Amber = approaching expiry (<14 days). Red = overdue — violation of service.yaml rotation_days. Vault event stream transitions from polled to push.
security_posture_controls.data_source: Prometheus scrape of secret_expiry_seconds gauge + Vault/AWS Secrets Manager events

security_posture_controls.name: Blast Radius Visualiser
security_posture_controls.description: Click any service to see: upstream (what data it has access to) and downstream (what an attacker could reach). Uses dependency graph from service.yaml — criticality field (hard/soft) determines immediate failure vs degradation.

security_posture_controls.name: CVE Exposure Badges
security_posture_controls.description: Snyk/Dependabot/Trivy results piped to Observability Aggregator via webhook. Each service shows critical/high CVE count. CVE on services with data_classification pii or financial triggers elevated SIEM alerts. Updated on deploy, not continuously.

security_posture_controls.name: Audit Log Separation
security_posture_controls.description: Payment, IAM, KYC/AML, admin, and config change logs go to separate WORM pipeline. 100% capture, 7yr retention, immutable, auditor-only access. Engineers excluded. Dashboard gets read-only compliance summary only. S3 Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode (not GOVERNANCE — GOVERNANCE allows privileged delete).
security_posture_controls.enforcement: Audit Log Store (SVC-111) + S3 Object Lock COMPLIANCE mode

service_to_service_auth.token_propagation: JWT with service identity claims propagated via Authorization header
service_to_service_auth.policy_enforcement: Istio AuthorizationPolicy resources generated from service.yaml allowed-call declarations

exceptions.pair: External payment rails (SWIFT, FPS, BACS, CHAPS)
exceptions.rationale: External systems use their own auth standards

additional_controls: Never log full PAN or CVV

levels.description: Data subject to specific regulatory handling

per_service_classification.justification: Holds customer credentials, session data, SM&CR mappings
CDD records, SAR filings, PEP screening results
Portfolio positions, investment advice records (MiFID II)
Message headers only — payloads classified per topic
Telemetry data with PII scrubbing applied

zones.name: Data Zone
services: All databases, Event Bus, Data Platform
zones.access: Application zone only, no direct external access

zones.name: Compliance Zone
zones.access: Restricted access, auditor-only for audit store

design_decisions.decision: Zero-trust model with service.yaml as authoritative allowed-call policy source
design_decisions.rationale: service.yaml is version-controlled and code-reviewed. Istio enforces at runtime. Diff between policy and observed calls is a security signal — not just a configuration artefact.
design_decisions.rejected_because: Network-only cannot enforce service-level granularity. Manual rules drift from reality.

design_decisions.decision: Data classification drives SIEM alert severity — CVE on a pii/financial service triggers elevated alert
design_decisions.rationale: Not all vulnerabilities are equal. A CVE in the notification service is less urgent than the same CVE in KYC/AML. data_classification in service.yaml enables automated triage.
design_decisions.rejected_because: Alert fatigue. Uniform severity means critical findings on regulated services get the same attention as low-risk services.

design_decisions.decision: S3 Object Lock COMPLIANCE mode for audit store — not GOVERNANCE mode
design_decisions.rationale: GOVERNANCE mode allows a privileged user to delete objects, defeating WORM requirement. COMPLIANCE mode makes objects immutable for the retention period — even root/admin cannot delete. Required for PCI Req 10, MLR 2017 Reg 40, SM&CR accountability.
design_decisions.rejected_because: Regulatory requirement is immutability, not access control. A sufficiently privileged user bypassing GOVERNANCE mode is exactly the threat model audit logs protect against.
